title: Cohorted interleaving experiment planner with drift-adaptation and safe rollback
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Problem statement:
We need an experiment controller that supports cohorted interleaving (fine-grained alternation of request assignment across model variants) to reduce confounding from time-varying traffic and to improve statistical power for short-lived canaries. This controller should adapt exposure dynamically when cohort drift is detected, run robust sequential statistical checks, and integrate with Redwood Console to perform automated rollback or graduated exposure changes when safety thresholds are breached.

Goals:
- Provide a prescriptive experiment setup flow for product and infra teams to run short canaries (minutes-hours) and multi-day A/Bs using the same primitives.
- Improve signal-to-noise for low-traffic cohorts by interleaving requests across variants at the session or request boundary.
- Detect distributional drift (cohort drift) quickly and reduce exposure automatically to avoid spurious conclusions.
- Implement sequential hypothesis tests (alpha-spending + Bayesian continuous monitoring fallback) to allow early stop decisions while controlling false positive rate.
- Wire automatic rollback triggers into Console runbooks and create an audit trail for every automated action.

Proposed design (high level):
- Experiment spec: cohorts, interleaving window (N requests or T seconds), primary/secondary metrics, min-run-size, min-conversions, maximum exposure schedule.
- Assignment algorithm: deterministic interleaver keyed by session_id/user_id/time-slice so assignments are reproducible for debugging and replay. Support both per-request and per-session modes.
- Drift monitor: per-cohort distribution tests (KS for continuous features, chi-square for categorical buckets), and embedding-based distance checks for prompt / user-text distributions; if drift exceeds a threshold for M consecutive windows, throttle variant exposure by a configurable factor (50% reduction default).
- Sequential checks: implement an alpha-spending wrapper around two test families: (1) frequentist z-test with O'Brien-Fleming-like spending for binary/ratio metrics, (2) Bayesian beta-Bernoulli online test for low-count metrics. Tests can run in parallel and feed a composite decision rule.
- Safety rules & rollback: define three classes of triggers — Signal-level (stat threshold), Product-impact (critical metric delta beyond X%), and Infrastructure (latency/500-rate spike). An automated runbook will attempt a staged rollback (50% -> 10% -> 0%) with pauses and Slack/Teams + Console alerts. All actions are recorded and reversible.
- Observability: time series and cohort breakdowns in Console, per-variant causal lift visualization, statistical annotations (p-value, CI, posterior probability), and a downloadable experiment snapshot for audits.

Why different from existing frameworks in repo:
Many existing tickets focus on exposure controllers and adaptive cohorts, but this approach centers on deterministic interleaving to maximize comparability inside short windows, plus a drift thermostat that actively reduces exposure rather than full aborts on noisy signals. The combination of interleaving + robust sequential tests is aimed at short-lived canaries where conventional A/B tooling underperforms.
acceptance_criteria: Users can declare an interleaving experiment via the Console API with cohorts, interleaving mode, primary metric, and exposure schedule
Assignment is reproducible: given a snapshot id and seed, we can deterministically replay variant assignments for any request timestamp
Drift monitor triggers a configurable exposure reduction and posts a Console alert; exposure change is enacted automatically when configured
Sequential test runs produce the decision outcome (continue/stop/rollback) with annotated statistics and the system honors alpha spending parameters
Automated rollback runbook will execute staged rollbacks and append audit events to the experiment timeline; manual override available
End-to-end integration tests exist (experiment creation -> traffic assignment -> drift event -> automated reduction -> rollback) with synthetic traffic harness
